properties.name: The implementing agent holds a compact design reference for the black box under work — its function, constraints, ports and the far side of each port — derived from the graph, the way a coder holds pseudocode; never the whole design
properties.statement:
Anthony, 2026-09-13, sharpening the pseudo-design brainstorm: "It isn't just a view/rendering, it is a reference for the person writing the code. What I'm getting at is some design reference that the AI agent can always refer to … a layer that the agent implementing the design can easily always reference. This is for the AI agent, not a rendered product for the human."

REVISED THE SAME DAY, ON HIS WORD, TO FIX THE UNIT (chg:the-design-reference-is-scoped-to-the-black-box-under-work): "In a large design, I'm not sure [re-injecting the design] is a good idea. Say I was designing an exhaust manifold for an engine of a car and the manifold was taking a long time — I don't think it'd be appropriate to say, here is the whole car design again. It may be more appropriate that the neighbourhood of the design was re-injected. Or in terms of systems engineering, maybe its black box and interface were injected. That may help keep the AI agent focused and not flood context with a lot of non-relevant information."

WHAT IS REQUIRED. reflow2 serves, for THE BLACK BOX UNDER WORK, one compact reference for the implementing agent: the requirements that box must satisfy; its capabilities as function headers (name, what each takes in and gives out — the signature); the constraints and governed rules that bind it, with their units and their consequence; its ports — every interface it provides or consumes, named even where the contract is still unspecified — and, for each port, the far side: the black box on the other end as a header only, never its insides. The parent's contract is included because the box must fit it; siblings appear only through shared ports. The whole design is NEVER the unit: the manifold's reference holds the manifold, the engine's contract it must fit, and the pipes it bolts to — not the car. It is DERIVED from the graph on every read, never hand-maintained, so it cannot drift; CODE-SHAPED rather than prose; and small BY CONSTRUCTION, because the region bounds it, so the agent refers to it continuously rather than fetching pieces by id. The region is the same computation claims and scoped gap detection already use — a seed's containment closure plus a propagation radius — and the reply says what it left out, so a narrowed reference never reads as the whole. The agent building against it is the expected use, not a human reading it.

WHY THIS SHAPE, in the benefits he relayed from SudoLang's own material (claims as stated by its sources, not verified here): a structured, code-like form puts a language model in a higher-reasoning "code mode", reported as 10–15% more accurate than natural-language prompts; "referential omnipotence" — a function is inferred from its name and description without an implementation, which is exactly what a capability signature is; constraint-based programming — declare rules that are continuously obeyed rather than steps; and token efficiency — 20–30% fewer tokens than prose for the same logic. Whether those numbers hold for this reference is a measurement this project owes before claiming them (req:context-is-a-modelled-quantity was dropped precisely for asserting design-time token estimates).

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is not read as new machinery: req:intent-is-reinjected (proposed 2026-07-28, never accepted) asks that design intent be read back into a long build on a counter and on symptoms of drift, and named no payload — THIS IS ITS PAYLOAD, and the scoping above answers its worry about flooding a long session. The capability signature setter exists (cap:a-capability-states-what-it-takes-and-gives) and is set on 3 of 247. claim_region and scoped detect_gaps already compute a neighbourhood. What does not exist is the one compact, agent-facing form for a box and the instruction that the agent builds against it.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BECOME: the whole design re-injected; a second hand-edited serialization that drifts from the schema; a rendering for a person (that is the SV-1/SV-4 view, a different deliverable); or a new language with a grammar — SudoLang's own claim is that models understand structured natural language with constraints unprompted, so the form is a rendering convention over the schema that already exists. Fill-ins are defects: every line traces to a node.
